correctness.rationale: For each cyclic root set of size k the exact map count is k! k n^(n-k-1). Gamma integration of (1-z)^s(1+z)^(n-s) gives a polynomial derivative whose factored integrand is pointwise negative when s is odd, s>=n/2. The s=n boundary cancels its apparent denominator. The spectral multiplicity count is binomial; finite self-map checker independently confirms boundary and formula.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The classical uniform cyclic-set decomposition gives the weights k! k n^(n-k-1), so it implies an exact finite sum for the transform. To conclude strict negativity for every odd s>=n/2 still requires the sign-controlled factorial integral. The prior conditional-component results do not cover this inequality.
